title: fix(runtime): the run-lifecycle refusal names only a remedy the tenancy posture honours (#19874)
body:
Fixes #19874
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`POST /automation/:name/runs/:runId/cancel` and `.../restore-suspension` admit only the ADR-0095 `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung. Their refusal told every refused caller to obtain "the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant, ADR-0068 D2". Under a walled posture (`group` / `isolated`) the platform-admin derivation no longer reads that grant as an anchor. The resolver sets `legacyGrantAnchorRetired = postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())` and gates the grant route on it. So on a walled deployment the refusal named a remedy that fails silently.

The middle sentence of the refusal is now built from the inputs the derivation reads, using the same expression, `postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())`:

| requested posture | the refusal says platform-operator standing comes from |
|---|---|
| `group` / `isolated` | only the deployment's declared platform administrators: an account whose verified email address is listed in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` |
| `single` | an unscoped `admin_full_access` grant (ADR-0068 D2), or the declared administrators in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` |
| unreadable (`resolveTenancyPosture` throws) | the declared administrators in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` (honoured on every posture), without echoing the environment value |

- The first sentence (what the verbs are) and the last sentence (the `resume` door) are unchanged.
- The gate is unchanged. It is still `ec.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` plus the `isSystem` bypass, still `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, and admits the same callers on every arm. The posture read sits inside a guard, so it can change the wording but never the answer.
- `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` is quoted through `PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL_ENV` (`@objectstack/types`). That is the constant the boot-side walled lines in `plugin-security` already quote, and the name `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx` documents. The set name is quoted through `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS` (`@objectstack/spec/identity`), the constant the resolver compares against.
- `single` is described as it ships today and nothing more. The runtime string carries no tracker id and does not predict the `single` disposition. #11979 is not addressed here.

### Docblocks corrected (comment-only)

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`: the run-lifecycle gate docblock said the rung "is derived from the unscoped `admin_full_access` evidence and nothing else". That is false. The config anchor confers on every posture, and walled postures retire the grant anchor. It now states the per-posture anchors, and notes that only the refusal sentence reads the posture while admission does not.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/activation-gate.ts:56`: the same sentence, word for word ("derived from the unscoped-grant evidence and nothing else"), corrected the same way. **This file is outside the claim's declared file surface.** It was fixed under os-dev's bounded in-place-fix exemption:
  - ① same defect class: the twin sentence.
  - ② mechanical, with the shape set by the `automation.ts` fix.
  - ③ no open PR touches the file: the file lists of all 17 open PRs were read.
  - ④ comment-only, so no new verification surface.

  The claim's file surface needs this path added. `activation-gate.ts:51` was left alone: it quotes the old premise and already says it "stopped holding", which is true.

### Sweep of `packages/runtime/src` (non-test)

Spellings searched: `` unscoped `admin_full_access` ``, `` admin_full_access` grant ``, `admin_full_access grant`, `unscoped grant`, `unscoped-grant`, `ADR-0068 D2`, `unscoped admin_full_access`. Every non-comment string line naming a platform operator or admin was also read.

- The only runtime string that prescribed the grant was this refusal (`automation.ts:656` on `3557f85f`).
- `activation-gate.ts:134` and `:237` say "platform operator" and name no mechanism, which is true on every posture.
- `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts:521` is ledger data about a vendor code, not a remedy.
- `route-ledger.ts` notes name the rung, not a remedy.

## Tests

New file: `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-run-lifecycle-deny-remedy.test.ts` (8 tests). It does not pin wording. For each of `single`, `group` and `isolated` it pins one equivalence: **the refusal names a remedy if and only if the resolver honours it**. For each candidate remedy, it builds a caller whose only route to standing is that remedy and resolves it through the runtime's own `resolveExecutionContext`, with the real core resolver underneath and the requested posture read from the environment as in production. It then hands that caller to the real dispatcher:

- If the resolver honours the remedy, the gate admits the caller (200, the verb called once). This is the lit control.
- If it does not, the caller is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` + 403 with the same sentence, which does not name that remedy. This is the mirror.
- A control table shows the grant fixture does resolve `PLATFORM_ADMIN` under `single`. So a walled `false` means the anchor is retired, not that the fixture is broken.
- A non-vacuity assertion checks that every posture's refusal names at least one working remedy.
- Also covered: both doors answer an identical sentence, and an unreadable posture keeps `PERMISSION_DENIED` + 403.

Reverse verification ran on `b4b3ed07` (fix and test committed first). Each mutation was applied with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit x1 to x0, blob changed) and ran under a trap. Each restore was proven: blob equal to the HEAD blob `daa4fa8562bf`, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean. The subject is imported through relative source paths, and runtime's vitest config aliases `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/types` and `@objectstack/spec` to `src`, so no `dist/` rebuild applies. Every run turned red as predicted:

| mutation | new suite |
|---|---|
| the pre-fix sentence restored as the middle part | **7 of 8 red**. The pre-existing door suite (38 tests) stays green under it, so the old suite could not see this defect. The "both doors" row stays green, as expected: it pins sameness, not content. |
| the walled arm also names the grant | **2 red**: the `group` and `isolated` equivalence rows, "grant: named ⇔ honoured: expected true to be false" |
| the `single` arm stops naming the grant | **1 red**: the `single` row, "expected false to be true" |
| the posture read left unguarded | **1 red**: the unreadable-posture row |

## Local verification (at `40bf21c9`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local` (the `test` script's project): **277 files passed, 3901 tests passed, 1 skipped**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0. This covers `tsc --noEmit` and `check:test-typecheck`, which held the ledger at 27 files, 191 errors and 69 pinned signatures. The new test is inside `tsconfig.test.json`'s program (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit).
- `pnpm lint` (full `eslint . --no-inline-config` union): exit 0.
- `dispatch-gates --commands` on the real diff derived the same 60 commands as the PM's list. Result: **58 exit 0, 2 NOT MEASURED**. `--ran` reconciliation: "60 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 58 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)". This includes `pnpm check:doc-authoring`: "sibling-package prose ids hold the baseline — 816 pinned site(s) across 231 file(s) ... no growth, no burn-down unrecorded". `scripts/doc-authoring-prose-id.baseline.json` is unchanged, and `automation.ts` never had an entry in it.
- Also run, exit 0: the five roster gates whose rosters sit beside these paths (`check-changeset-fixed`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:route-ledger-census`), and `check-issue-citations --base 3557f85f` ("every citation this change adds resolves").
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`**. Reason: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. It is a whole-tree gate, and 39 packages have no `dist/`. A narrowed substitute ran for runtime only: after the build, `require('@objectstack/runtime')` in a real node process resolved `dist/index.cjs` (exit 0, 260 exports). `dist/index.cjs` carries the new sentence (1 hit) and not the old one (0 hits). This is a substitute, not the gate.
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:type-check-debt`**. Reason: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (`@objectstack/driver-turso` has no built type entry). Runtime's own typecheck above is the per-package half.
- Declared to CI: runtime's `test:repo` project, and the families that take workflow values.

## Acceptance notes

- `check:doc-authoring`: the card said this message sits "under the shrink-only `check:doc-authoring` baseline". Measured, that is not the case. That gate's runtime leg is a (file, tracker-id) ratchet over string literals. The old message carried no tracker id, and `automation.ts` has no baseline entry. Editing the message owes the baseline nothing as long as no `#NNNN` enters a string. The new strings carry ADR ids only.
- Stale comments, noted and not filed (comment drift, outside this claim; carrier: none):
  - `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`: the §6d comment (about lines 1042-1045) and the `hasPlatformAdminStanding` docblock (about lines 1085-1098) still say `PLATFORM_ADMIN` derives from the unscoped-grant evidence "and nothing else". That file is read-only in this lane.
  - `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts:178` says "derives only from an unscoped admin_full_access grant".
  - `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-run-lifecycle-door.test.ts:117`: the `OPERATOR_CTX` doc comment says "derived from the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant".
- Route choice: the suggested route was one posture-neutral sentence with a `single` qualifier. That sentence would still name the grant on a walled deployment. The qualifier "until #11979 decides otherwise" would also put a tracker id into a runtime string and predict that card's outcome. A config-only sentence would be true everywhere. But it would describe `single` as config-only, which is the reading the `single` disposition ruling reversed. So the sentence is chosen per posture, using the derivation's own expression.
